name: J. R. R. Tolkien
bio: Oxford philologist and architect of Middle-earth whose invented languages and mythic history reshaped modern fantasy. Tolkien's work is rooted in scholarship, war memory, and a deep love of northern legend—not in film spectacle.

works.title: The Hobbit
works.blurb: A quest tale of unexpected courage, dragons, and the road that goes ever on, written first for children and lasting for everyone.

works.title: The Lord of the Rings
works.blurb: An epic of fellowship, power, and pity whose secondary world is built from language outward.

works.title: The Silmarillion
works.blurb: The deep mythic history of the Elder Days—creation, exile, and ruin—edited from Tolkien's lifelong legendarium.

significance: Foundational architect of modern high fantasy through language-first worldbuilding.
fact: A professional philologist whose invented tongues preceded and shaped his narratives.
quote: Not all those who wander are lost.
visualConcept: Hand-drawn map zooming into legend (no film look)

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for J. R. R. Tolkien
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate (not a photograph). Portrait rights generally controlled by the Tolkien Estate; plate is original.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
fullName: Gabriel José de la Concordia García Márquez
bio: Colombian Nobel laureate who made Macondo a global grammar for memory, solitude, and the marvelous ordinary. García Márquez fused journalism's clarity with mythic exaggeration.

works.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
works.blurb: The multi-generational saga of the Buendía family and the town of Macondo—magical realism's most famous cathedral.

works.title: Love in the Time of Cholera
works.blurb: A decades-long love story of patience, pride, and the comedy of desire beside the Caribbean.

works.title: Chronicle of a Death Foretold
works.blurb: A spare, circular chronicle of a murder everyone saw coming and no one stopped.

significance: Central voice of the Latin American Boom and Nobel Prize in Literature (1982).
fact: Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.
quote: What matters in life is not what happens to you but what you remember and how you remember it.
visualConcept: Ordinary objects tipping into the impossible

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for Gabriel García Márquez
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate (not a photograph). Many press photos remain under copyright; plate is original.

name: Miguel de Cervantes
bio: Soldier, captive, and inventor of the modern novel. Cervantes's Don Quixote turned idealism and parody into a new form of fiction that still frames how we read character and reality.

works.title: Don Quixote
works.blurb: The knight of the sorrowful countenance rides out into a world that refuses to match his books—comedy, cruelty, and metafiction at once.

works.title: Novelas Ejemplares
works.blurb: A set of exemplary novellas ranging from picaresque grit to romance, showcasing Cervantes's range beyond the Quixote.

works.title: La Galatea
works.blurb: An early pastoral romance that reveals Cervantes's first long experiments with narrative desire.

significance: Foundational author of the modern European novel.
fact: Don Quixote appeared in two parts (1605 and 1615) and helped invent metafictional play.
quote: The truth may be stretched thin, but it never breaks.

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for Miguel de Cervantes
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate. Attributed historical portraits (e.g. Jáuregui) are public domain on Wikimedia Commons.

sources.label: Cervantes scholarship / Biblioteca Nacional de España

name: Charles Dickens
bio: Victorian novelist of fog, factories, and feeling whose serial fiction made social conscience popular entertainment. Dickens gave the city a moral weather system.

works.title: Oliver Twist
works.blurb: A workhouse orphan's path through crime and kindness, exposing the cruelty of institutions that claim to care.

works.title: A Christmas Carol
works.blurb: Scrooge's night of ghosts remains the language of seasonal redemption and social responsibility.

works.title: Great Expectations
works.blurb: Pip's rise and shame form a novel of class, guilt, and the true sources of gentility.

significance: Defining novelist of Victorian London and serial social fiction.
fact: Published most major novels in serial parts, shaping how readers awaited story.
quote: No one is useless in this world who lightens the burdens of another.

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for Charles Dickens
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate. Public-domain photographs (e.g. Jeremiah Gurney) on Wikimedia Commons.

name: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
fullName: Antoine Marie Jean-Baptiste Roger de Saint-Exupéry
bio: Aviator-writer whose desert crashes and night mail routes became philosophy. Saint-Exupéry wrote of responsibility, friendship, and the sky—without relying on copyrighted Little Prince illustrations.

works.title: The Little Prince
works.blurb: A fable of planets, roses, and tamed foxes that asks adults to remember what essential things are invisible to the eye.

works.title: Night Flight
works.blurb: A taut novel of airmail pilots racing storms and duty across South American nights.

works.title: Wind, Sand and Stars
works.blurb: Memoir-essays of flight, crash, and human solidarity under desert stars.

significance: Pilot-philosopher of modern French letters; The Little Prince is among the world's most translated books.
fact: Disappeared on a 1944 reconnaissance mission over the Mediterranean.
quote: What is essential is invisible to the eye.
visualConcept: Rise from desert sand into open sky (no copyrighted art)
notes: Do not use copyrighted Little Prince artwork.

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate (not copyrighted Little Prince art). Historical photos: Wikimedia Commons category.

name: George Orwell
bio: Essayist and novelist of clarity against tyranny. As George Orwell, Eric Blair made political writing an art and warned how language itself can be occupied.

works.title: Animal Farm
works.blurb: A fable of revolution betrayed, where some animals become more equal than others.

works.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
works.blurb: A dystopia of surveillance, Newspeak, and the erasure of truth that still names our political nightmares.

works.title: Homage to Catalonia
works.blurb: Orwell's firsthand account of the Spanish Civil War and the fractures inside the left.

significance: Moral stylist of anti-totalitarian literature and political English prose.
fact: Took the pen name George Orwell; fought in Spain and later wrote against both fascism and Stalinism.
quote: In a time of deceit telling the truth is a revolutionary act.

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for George Orwell
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate. Some press images remain restricted; plate is original. See Orwell Foundation.

sources.label: Orwell Foundation / public domain editions (where applicable)

name: Ernest Hemingway
bio: Master of stripped prose and iceberg understatement. Hemingway wrote war, love, and courage as surfaces that hide vast depths.

works.title: The Sun Also Rises
works.blurb: Expatriates drift from Paris to Pamplona in a novel of wound, ritual, and the Lost Generation.

works.title: A Farewell to Arms
works.blurb: A love story against the Italian front, where war unmakes every private vow.

works.title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
works.blurb: An American in the Spanish Civil War learns that no one is an island—and that bridges are costly.

significance: Architect of modernist spareness; Nobel Prize in Literature (1954).
fact: Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.
quote: There is nothing to writing. All you do is sit down at a typewriter and bleed.
visualConcept: Prose stripped to a single horizon line

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for Ernest Hemingway
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate. Several public-domain photographs exist on Wikimedia Commons (Category:Ernest Hemingway).

name: Leo Tolstoy
bio: Russian novelist of war, marriage, and spiritual crisis whose epics expanded what fiction could hold. Tolstoy sought truth in both panorama and the deathbed of a single soul.

works.title: War and Peace
works.blurb: A vast novel of Napoleonic invasion, family life, and the mystery of historical force.

works.title: Anna Karenina
works.blurb: Adultery, society, and the search for a meaningful life—Tolstoy's most intimate epic.

works.title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
works.blurb: A novella of a bureaucrat's dying that strips away false living with merciless clarity.

significance: Summit of the nineteenth-century realist novel and moral inquiry.
fact: Lived and wrote at Yasnaya Polyana; later embraced radical Christian ethics and pacifism.
quote: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
visualConcept: Horizon expanding across steppe and war

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for Leo Tolstoy
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate. Public-domain photographs (incl. Prokudin-Gorsky) on Wikimedia Commons.

name: William Shakespeare
bio: The English stage's central imagination—tragedy, comedy, history, and sonnets that still supply our language for love, ambition, and doubt.

works.title: Hamlet
works.blurb: A prince's delayed revenge becomes a meditation on thought, theater, and mortality.

works.title: Romeo and Juliet
works.blurb: Youthful love against a feud, written in heat and lyric speed.

works.title: Macbeth
works.blurb: Ambition, prophecy, and blood—Scotland's night collapsing under a usurper's guilt.

significance: Cornerstone of English-language drama and poetic vocabulary.
fact: Associated with the Lord Chamberlain's / King's Men and the Globe Theatre.
quote: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for William Shakespeare
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate. Droeshout engraving (First Folio) is public domain on Wikimedia Commons.

name: J. K. Rowling
bio: British novelist whose Harry Potter series returned global childhood reading to long-form wonder. This gallery focuses on literary craft and book history—not film or theme-park iconography.

works.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
works.blurb: A cupboard under the stairs opens onto a school of magic and a war waiting in memory.

works.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
works.blurb: Time, loyalty, and fear take adult shape as the series darkens with craft and consequence.

works.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
works.blurb: The final hunt for Horcruxes closes the bildungsroman as epic of sacrifice and choice.

significance: Late-twentieth-century phenomenon that revived reading culture for a generation.
fact: First novel published in 1997 (UK) as Philosopher's Stone; series completed in 2007.
quote: It is our choices, Harry, that show what we truly are, far more than our abilities.
visualConcept: Pages turning into an archive shelf (no Hogwarts/movie look)

portrait.alt: Illustrative museum plate for J. K. Rowling (not a photograph)
portrait.credit: Illustrative museum plate / silhouette — living author; no photographic likeness claimed. Rights unclear for press photos.
